Abducted by her uncle Hades and made queen of the underworld, this daughter of Zeus and Demeter personifies the return of spring each year — who is she?
Persephone: Greek goddess of spring and the queen of the underworld.

After eight years in UN-funded public health work, this Indian strategist helped re-elect Narendra Modi as Gujarat's chief minister in 2012 before founding his own party ahead of the 2025 Bihar election — who is he?
Prashant Kishor: Indian politician. Prashant Kishor (born 20 March 1977), colloquially known as PK, is an Indian politician, the founder of the Jan Suraaj Party and a former political strategist.
A Baptist minister and close friend of Martin Luther King Jr., he helped launch the Montgomery bus boycott and took over the SCLC after King's assassination. Who was he?
Ralph Abernathy: American activist and minister (1926–1990)
This Easy Company paratrooper earned the Distinguished Service Cross for his assault on Brécourt Manor during D-Day, and was later played by Damian Lewis in a hit HBO miniseries — who was he?
Richard Winters: United States Army officer and veteran (1918–2011)
This Japanese politician has served in the House of Councillors for the Liberal Democratic Party after stints as Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Defense and of the Cabinet Office — who is she?
A former partisan and socialist politician, this journalist-turned-statesman served as president of Italy from 1978 to 1985 — who is he?
Sandro Pertini: President of Italy from 1978 to 1985.
Serving as his country's foreign minister since 2004 — longer than anyone since the Soviet era — this diplomat also speaks fluent Sinhala and Dhivehi from his early postings — who is he?
This legendary Germanic hero slew the dragon Fafnir and was later murdered after a quarrel involving his wife and another woman he had unknowingly helped deceive — who is he?
This leading man of 1950s Westerns and film noir later played General Jack D. Ripper in Dr. Strangelove and Captain McCluskey in The Godfather — who is he?

As senior counselor to a Tokugawa shōgun, this Edo-period official pursued reforms that debased the currency and sold monopoly rights to merchants — remembered for both economic innovation and rampant corruption — who was he?
Tanuma Okitsugu: Japanese political advisor, rōjū (1719–1788)
Sparked by tensions over Colombia's 1886 constitution and the Regeneración, this conflict pitted Liberals against a Conservative government from October 1899 to November 1902 — which conflict?
Thousand Days' War: Civil war in Colombia from 1899 to 1902. It would end three years later with the signing of the Treaty of Neerlandia and the Treaty of Wisconsin.

Proclaimed by the Central Council after the October Revolution and formally independent from Russia by January 1918, what short-lived Eastern European state emerged from the collapsing Russian Empire?
Ukrainian People's Republic: 1917–18/1918–21 state in Eastern Europe.
Once governor of Donetsk Oblast, this pro-Russian politician served as Ukraine's fourth president until the 2014 Revolution of Dignity drove him into exile in Russia — who is he?
Viktor Yanukovych: President of Ukraine from 2010 to 2014.
What is this — “2021 vehicular mass murder in Wisconsin”?
Waukesha Christmas parade attack: 2021 vehicular mass murder in Wisconsin. The parade was live-streamed, and other attendees captured the incident on videos later posted to social media.
Raging from 1914 to 1918 and nicknamed 'the Great War,' this conflict's mass troop movements helped spread the deadly Spanish flu pandemic — which war?
World War I: 1914–1918 global conflict. The war saw important developments in weaponry including tanks, aircraft, artillery, machine guns, and chemical weapons.

Rooted mostly among rural Indigenous communities in Chiapas, this Mexican far-left group has been in a frozen conflict with the state since 1994 and takes its name from a revolutionary agrarian commander — which group?
Zapatista Army of National Liberation: Far-left political and militant group in southern Mexico.
Which one below was born first?
George Grove (born 1820) is the earliest of the four. Grove was trained as a civil engineer, and successful in that profession, but his love of music drew him into musical administration.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
Earth (formed ~4.54 billion years ago) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is an astronomer?
Frank Kameny is an astronomer. Franklin Edward Kameny (May 21, 1925 – October 11, 2011) was an American gay rights activist.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Eugene Wigner is a mathematician. Wigner and Hermann Weyl were responsible for introducing group theory into physics, particularly the theory of symmetry in physics.
What is the atomic number of Seaborgium?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
What is the atomic number of Bromine?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
In what year was Abraham Maslow born?
Abraham Maslow: Maslow was a psychology professor at Cornell University, Brooklyn College, Brandeis University, The New School for Social Research, and Columbia University.
In what year was Larry Page born?
Larry Page: Lawrence Edward Page (born March 26, 1973) is an American businessman and computer scientist who co-founded Google with Sergey Brin.
In what year was Alexey Pajitnov born?
Alexey Pajitnov: Alexey Leonidovich Pajitnov (born April 16, 1955) is a Russian and American computer engineer and video game designer.
In what year did Omar Khayyam die?
Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
In what year did James Clerk Maxwell die?
James Clerk Maxwell: Maxwell's equations for electromagnetism achieved the second great unification in physics, where the first one had been realised by Isaac Newton.
In what year was Sodium discovered?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Ammonium chloride: Pfizer. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet E2 family based?
Embraer E-Jet E2 family: Brazil. The Embraer E-Jet E2 family is a series of four-abreast narrow-body regional jet airliners designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer.
Who is credited with discovering Lynx?
Lynx (constellation): Johannes Hevelius. Lynx is a constellation named after the animal, usually observed in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Newton's law of universal gravitation?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Robert Hooke. This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.
Who is credited with discovering Pulsar?
Pulsar: Jocelyn Bell Burnell. This produces a very precise interval between pulses that ranges from milliseconds to seconds for an individual pulsar.
Who is credited with discovering Coma Berenices?
Coma Berenices: Conon of Samos. Coma Berenices is an ancient asterism in the northern sky, which has been defined as one of the 88 modern constellations.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.

Affecting roughly 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder impairs the nervous system, causing severe intellectual disability and little to no speech, but is also linked to an unusually happy demeanor — what's it called?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.
This South Korean actress started as a child model in 2005 and later starred in the popular series True Beauty. Who is she?
Arrhythmia are irregularities in the heartbeat, including when it is too fast or too slow.
Nicknamed 'Red-Stockings,' this French herding dog breed hails from the plains of Central France — which breed is it?
Beauceron (French) is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France.
Around 2,500 species of this insect family defend themselves by secreting a skin-irritating toxin called cantharidin, often flaunting bold warning colors — which family?
Blister beetle are beetles of the family Meloidae, so called for their defensive secretion of a blistering agent, cantharidin.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
Seen as the frontman of Mexican neoliberalism, this economist-president championed and signed NAFTA after an election clouded by fraud accusations — who is he?
Carlos Salinas de Gortari (Spanish; born 3 April 1948) is a Mexican economist and former politician who served as the 60th president of Mexico from 1988 to 1994.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

Ranging across most of Europe and into the Palearctic as far as northwestern China, this medium-sized bird of prey sees its northernmost populations migrate as far as South Africa each winter — which raptor?
Common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.
Discovered to have two undescribed relatives only in 2019, this Amazonian 'knifefish' is best known for generating powerful electric discharges — which species?
Electrophorus electricus is the best-known species of electric eel. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This Hungarian-American physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus, having once worked as an assistant to David Hilbert at Göttingen. Who was he?
Eugene Wigner (November 17, 1902 - January 1, 1995) was a Hungarian-American theoretical physicist who also contributed to mathematical physics.

This region of the upper limb, running between the elbow and the wrist, contains two long bones, the radius and the ulna, and is technically distinct from the 'arm' proper in anatomy — what is it called?
Forearm is the region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist. It is homologous to the region of the leg that lies between the knee and the ankle joints, the crus.

Sharing the 1988 Nobel Prize, this American biochemist pioneered rational drug design — studying a drug's target rather than relying on trial and error — and her work led to AZT, the first widely used AIDS drug. Who was she?
Gertrude B. Elion (January 23, 1918 - February 21, 1999) was an American biochemist and pharmacologist, who shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with George H. Hitchings.

Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, this non-cancerous condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men and can occur in newborns, adolescents, and older or obese men — name the condition?

Gynecomastia (also spelled gynaecomastia) is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens.
With species ranging from evergreen trees to climbing shrubs across the tropics and temperate zones, this genus's most iconic species decorates Christmas cards worldwide — what genus is it?
Holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats pain, fever, and inflammation — from migraines to arthritis — and typically starts working within an hour, whether taken orally or intravenously. What drug?
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.

This American scientist co-authored a landmark 1953 paper with Francis Crick proposing the double-helix structure of DNA, building on research by Rosalind Franklin, and shared a 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery — who is he?
James Watson (April 6, 1928 - November 6, 2025) was an American molecular biologist, geneticist, and zoologist.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

Spread by the bite of sandflies and caused by a genus of protozoal parasites, this tropical disease can present as skin ulcers, disfiguring mucosal damage, or a more dangerous internal form. Name the disease?
Leishmaniasis is a wide array of clinical manifestations caused by protozoal parasites of the Trypanosomatida genus Leishmania.
Named for antennae often longer than its own body, this insect family boasts over 35,000 species and gets its name from a Greek myth about a shepherd transformed after angering nymphs — which group?
Longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species described.
This computer scientist led the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo Guidance Computer and is credited with coining the very term 'software engineering' — who is she?
Margaret Hamilton (software engineer) (ne Heafield; born August 17, 1936) is an American computer scientist.
This field's founding body, the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, grew out of an 1875 convention and eventually gave the world the International System of Units — what is this study called?
Metrology is the scientific study of measurement.
This small green legume, cultivated widely across East and South Asia, is used in both savory dishes and sweet desserts — what is it?
Mung bean (Vigna radiata) is a plant species in the legume family.
Born in the Austro-Hungarian Empire and emigrating to the US in 1884, he's known for pioneering the AC electricity system. Who?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 - 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
Chemists still debate the exact definition, but generally, any large molecule containing a carbon-hydrogen or carbon-carbon bond falls into this broad class of compounds. What is it?
Organic compound are a subclass of chemical compounds of carbon.

The males of this Phasianidae bird are famed for piercing calls and extravagant plumage; its Asiatic species include blue, green, and a third found only in the Congo Basin — what is this bird, collectively?

Peafowl is a common name for two bird species of the genus Pavo and one species of the closely related genus Afropavo within the tribe Pavonini of the family Phasianidae (the pheasants and their allies).

A pnictogen with only one stable isotope and atomic number 15, this element hides in Earth's crust mostly as phosphate rock and readily builds a vast family of organic and inorganic compounds. Which element is it?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Known as little hogweed or pursley, every part of this succulent plant can be eaten raw or cooked — what plant is it?
Portulaca oleracea (common purslane, also known as little hogweed, or pursley) is a succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae.
This kidney inflammation, most often caused by E. coli infection, typically causes fever and tenderness along the side of the body — what is it?
Pyelonephritis is inflammation of the kidney, typically due to a bacterial infection.
Home to about 200 species — among them the plants we call currants and gooseberries — this genus is the sole member of its own plant family — which genus?
Ribes is a genus of approximately 200 known species of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
The FAO/WHO Codex standard recognizes 21 species under this common name for small silvery forage fish, distinguished from their larger 'pilchard' cousins mainly by size — what fish is it?
Sardine are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.
First described in 1780, this slender, long-legged antelope of southern Africa wears a white face crossed by a dark stripe from eye to mouth — and both sexes sport backward-curving horns. What is it?
Springbok (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.

Caused by the spiral bacterium Treponema pallidum, this infection famously announces itself with a single painless ulcer called a chancre, then a rash that loves the palms and soles — which sexually transmitted disease is it?

Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum subspecies pallidum. The signs and symptoms depend on the stage it presents: primary, secondary, latent or tertiary.

Beloved by biologists for its wild morphological variation and elaborate nest-building, this northern fish tolerates big swings in salinity, living in the sea but breeding in fresh water — what is it?
Three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) is a fish native to most inland and coastal waters north of 30N.
An important food fish found in marine and brackish waters from the Baltic to the Mediterranean, this flatfish's Black Sea relatives are now classified as a separate species — which fish?
Turbot is a relatively large species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
Leading organic chemistry at DuPont's Experimental Station, this troubled chemist not only invented nylon but also helped lay the groundwork for neoprene. Who was he?
Wallace Carothers (April 27, 1896 - April 29, 1937) was an American chemist, inventor, and the leader of organic chemistry at DuPont, who was credited with the invention of nylon.

Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this Chinese strategist was sought out three times by a warlord before becoming chancellor of the Shu Han state and, later, regent to its young second emperor — who is he?

Zhuge Liang (181 AD - September or October 234 AD), courtesy name Kongming, was a Chinese statesman and strategist who lived through the collapse of the Eastern Han dynasty and became the principal architect of the Shu Han state.
This nucleoside, a building block of RNA, gives rise to the energy carriers ATP and ADP and is used as an intravenous drug for certain irregular heartbeats — what is it?
Working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer designed one of history's most famous puzzle games — yet saw no royalties from it until founding a company around it in 1996. Who is he?
Caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, this intestinal infection can spread to the liver and trigger abscesses there even without any prior diarrhea — what condition is it?
Amoebiasis: Human disease caused by amoeba protists.
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)

A physician who began writing stories while studying medicine in Edinburgh, he was knighted in 1902 and created both a famous consulting detective and the dinosaur-filled adventure The Lost World. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle: British writer and physician (1859–1930)
Nicknamed the hay bacterium for its soil habitat, this rod-shaped, spore-forming microbe is the best-studied Gram-positive species and a top industrial source of secreted enzymes — what is it?
Bacillus subtilis: Catalase-positive bacterium. It forms biofilms through the formation of extracellular polymeric matrix containing sugars and proteins.

With his former teacher Alfred North Whitehead, this English philosopher co-wrote Principia Mathematica and, alongside G. E. Moore, led the British 'revolt against idealism.' Who was this founder of analytic philosophy?
Bertrand Russell: English mathematician and philosopher (1872–1970)
Conceived for Pan Am as a jet two-and-a-half times the size of the 707, this wide-body, led by designer Joe Sutter, rolled out of the world's largest building in 1968 — which airliner is it?
Boeing 747: American wide-body four-engined jet long-range aircraft.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways typically causes a cough lasting around three weeks and is usually caused by a virus?
Bronchitis: Inflammation of the large airways in the lungs.
Originally defined as the heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius, this unit of energy in nutrition actually refers to a kilocalorie — what is it?

Calorie: Unit of energy used in nutrition. The small calorie or gram calorie is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius (or one kelvin).
Blending science, aesthetics, and technique, this discipline wrestles with projecting a round world onto flat media while deciding what details to keep or cut — what is it called?
Cartography: Study and practice of making maps.
Beyond the resistance-measuring "bridge" that carries his name, this English inventor also gave us the stereoscope, the English concertina, and the Playfair cipher — who was he?
Charles Wheatstone: English physicist and inventor (1802–1875)

Unlike oysters and mussels, which attach to a surface, or scallops, which live near the bottom, this bivalve mollusk instead burrows into sand or mud on the sea floor — what is it, the namesake of a popular chowder?
Clam: Common name for several kinds of bivalve mollusc.

This medium-sized bird of prey ranges across Europe into northwestern China, hunting rodents like voles from a perch, with northern populations migrating as far as South Africa for winter — what bird is this?
Common buzzard: Species of bird of prey. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit measures a material's ability to store electrical charge, equal to one coulomb per volt — what is it?
Farad: SI unit of electric capacitance.
Fluconazole: Antifungal medication. Fluconazole, sold under the brand name Diflucan among others, is an antifungal medication used for a number of fungal infections.
Named in 1753 from Greek words for 'milk' and 'flower,' this genus of about 20 bulbous perennial species is better known by its common name, snowdrop — what is its scientific genus?
Galanthus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Amaryllidacee.
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.

While working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow, this Scottish engineer's separate-condenser design transformed Newcomen's steam engine into the machine that powered the Industrial Revolution — who was he?
James Watt: Scottish inventor, engineer and chemist (1736–1819)

A Columbia economist and former World Bank chief economist who won the 2001 Nobel, he champions Georgism and skewers the "free-market fundamentalists" he blames for mismanaging globalization — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz: American economist and Nobel Laureate (born 1943)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.

One of the five big cats in the genus Panthera, this slender, muscular predator wears dark spots clustered into rosettes and is split today into eight recognised subspecies across Africa and Asia — what is it?
Leopard: Species of cat native to Africa and Asia.

A four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft, this American plane is a comprehensive update of an older transport design, with over 500 delivered to 26 operators worldwide as of 2022. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules: Military transport aircraft. The C-130J is a comprehensive update of the Lockheed C-130 Hercules, with new engines, flight deck, and other systems.
This is the common name for the larva of flies like houseflies and blowflies — though, confusingly, not for baby mosquitoes — what is it called?
This biological term covers the pairing of organisms for sexual reproduction, encompassing everything from copulation to external fertilization in fish and amphibians — what is it?
Mating: Process of pairing in biology.
Sold under the brand name Dolophine, this synthetic opioid is used to manage chronic pain and treat opioid use disorder by relieving cravings and withdrawal. What is it?
Methadone: Opioid analgesic and maintenance therapy.
Medically termed a 'spontaneous abortion,' this is the loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently — distinct from a stillbirth, which occurs after 20 weeks. What is it?
Miscarriage: Natural premature termination of pregnancy.

Made of contractile proteins called actin and myosin, this soft tissue exists in three vertebrate forms — skeletal, cardiac, and smooth — and forms during a developmental process called myogenesis — what is it?
Muscle: Important Biological tissue that allows movement.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Nicknamed 'brittle bone disease,' this genetic disorder causes fragile bones and blue-tinted eye whites, usually stemming from faulty type I collagen — what is it?
Osteogenesis imperfecta: Group of genetic disorders resulting in fragile bones.

Also called the blue passionflower, this South American vine climbs via tendrils to 10 metres, bears fragrant blue-white blooms with a fringed coronal filament, and produces an edible but not particularly tasty orange fruit — which plant is it?
Passiflora caerulea: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
Synthesized in 1938 by German chemist Otto Eisleb and later marketed as Demerol, this synthetic opioid was the go-to pain medication for much of the 20th century — what is it?
Pethidine: Opioid analgesic. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.

Not approved for general use in the US but sold across Europe for conditions such as vertigo and cortical myoclonus, this drug is a cyclic derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA and belongs to the 'racetam' group — what is it?
Domesticated some 7,000 to 10,000 years ago in what is now southern Peru, this starchy underground tuber belongs to the nightshade family — what is it?
Potato: Starchy tuber used as a staple food.
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

In this condition, tiny arteries spasm and starve the fingers of blood, classically turning them white, then blue, then a burning red as flow returns. It's named for the physician who first described it in 1862 — what is it?
Raynaud syndrome: Medical condition in which spasm of arteries causes episodes of reduced blood flow.
Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his tuberculosis research, this German physician's 1876 discovery of the anthrax bacterium is considered the birth of modern bacteriology — who is he?
Robert Koch: German physician and bacteriologist (1843–1910)
Held together by electrostatic forces called ionic bonds, this type of chemical compound pairs positive and negative ions into a substance with zero net charge — what class of compound?
Salt (chemistry): Chemical compound involving ionic bonding.

Discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named after the moon because of its resemblance to an element named for the Earth, this semiconductor finds use in glassmaking, pigments, and photocells — what element is it?
Selenium: Chemical element with atomic number 34 (Se)
The only species in its genus, this cosmopolitan pelagic fish from the mackerel family can grow past a metre long and matters hugely to global fisheries — which species?
Skipjack tuna: Species of fish. The skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a perciform fish in the tuna family, Scombridae, and is the only member of the genus Katsuwonus.

Once meaning a Christian life oriented toward the Holy Spirit, this concept broadened over centuries to describe a subjective sense of the sacred and 'the deepest values and meanings by which people live,' often apart from organized religion. What's the term?
NATO nicknamed this Soviet variable-sweep-wing tactical bomber 'Fencer'; it was the USSR's first plane with an integrated digital navigation-and-attack system — which aircraft is it?

Blockbuster (retailer): United States. The company expanded internationally throughout the 1990s.
This tire and rubber giant, headquartered in Tokyo's Kyōbashi district, has ranked as the world's second-largest tire manufacturer by revenue since 2021 and also makes golf equipment — which company?
Bridgestone (Kabushiki gaisha Burijisuton) is a Japanese multinational tire and rubber manufacturing company based in Kybashi, Tokyo.
One of the first companies ever listed on Nasdaq, this Santa Clara chipmaker helped develop the x86 instruction set found in most PCs — which company?
Intel is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

Known outside Ireland by one name but trading under a different one at home due to a trademark clash with an American retailer, this fast-fashion chain is owned by Associated British Foods — what retailer is it?
Primark (trading as Penneys in Ireland) is an Irish multinational retailer specialising in fast fashion.

This American businessman co-founded and served as CEO of a ride-hailing company from 2010 to 2017, resigning amid harassment allegations, and now runs a ghost-kitchen operator called CloudKitchens — who is he?
Travis Kalanick (born August 6, 1976) is an American businessman best known as the co-founder and former chief executive officer (CEO) of Uber.

Founded in 1961 by Gérard Mulliez, this French retail giant operates in Spain as Alcampo and in Russia as 'Ashan,' a name derived from the district of its very first store in Roubaix — what is this company called?
Auchan: French multinational retail company. Auchan (French: [oʃɑ̃]) is a French multinational retail group headquartered in Croix, France.
Founded in 1919 and now owned by Stellantis, this French automaker made its name in 1934 with the Traction Avant, the world's first mass-produced car of its kind — what's the brand?
Citroën: French car brand of Stellantis. Citroën (French: [sitʁɔɛn]) is a French automobile brand owned by Stellantis since 2021.
Founded in 1892 with divisions once spanning aerospace, energy, healthcare and finance, this American conglomerate underwent a major breakup in 2023 — which company?

Named after its founder Shōzō, this Tokyo-headquartered manufacturer builds everything from motorcycles and ships to aerospace and defense equipment, ranking among Japan's three biggest industrial conglomerates — which company?
Kawasaki Heavy Industries: Japanese multinational manufacturing company.
Founded in 1979 by the Weinstein brothers, this indie film powerhouse was acquired by Disney in 1993 and later sold to a Qatari-backed holding company — which studio?
Miramax: American film and television production and distribution company.

Founded in England in 1958 as a spinoff of a Bolton sporting-goods firm, this brand flew the Union Jack in its logo before being sold first to a German rival and later to Authentic Brands Group — name it?
Reebok: American footwear and clothing company.
Founded in 1899 and headquartered in Osaka, this Japanese drinks giant became a global player after acquiring Jim Beam's parent company in 2014 — which company?
Suntory: Japanese beverage company. Suntory Holdings Limited is a Japanese multinational brewing and distilling company.

A Russian tech company with 72% market share in its home country's search space and the largest ridesharing service there—but founded in 1997 to handle information differently. What is this Russian tech giant?
Yandex: Russian technology company. Yandex Search is the largest search engine in Russia with an estimated 72% market share in Russia and a 2.8% market share worldwide.
